title: Home Mortgage Loans: Adjustable-Rate Changes and Payment Re-Amortization
content:
# Home Mortgage Loans: Adjustable-Rate Changes and Payment Re-Amortization

This calculation guide covers how the note rate of an adjustable loan under Home Mortgage Loans is reset, the limits on each reset, how the monthly payment follows the new rate, and the notice owed to the borrower.

## Which loans change rate

A loan changes rate only if its program's rate type is adjustable. A loan in a fixed-rate program keeps its note rate for its whole term.

## When the rate changes

The starting rate stays fixed for the program's initial fixed period, measured in months from the first installment. After that, the rate changes once every adjustment interval of the program, each time on the loan's next scheduled change date.

## What the new rate is

**Fully indexed value.** On a change date, the candidate rate is the program's index as published 45 days before that change date, increased by the program's margin, and then rounded to the nearest 0.125 of a percentage point.

**Limits on the change.**
- At the first adjustment, the rate may move from its prior level by no more than the program's first-change cap.
- At every later adjustment, it may move by no more than the program's later-change cap.
- At no time may the rate be higher than the starting rate increased by the program's lifetime cap, and at no time may it be lower than the program's margin.

The new note rate is the rounded candidate rate, held within those limits.

**Payment.** After each change, the monthly principal-and-interest payment is re-amortized at the new rate over the term that remains.

**Notice.** The borrower is sent notice of the change no later than the program's notice period before the first payment falling due at the new rate.

## Worked adjustment (all inputs hypothetical)

Imagined terms, chosen only for the arithmetic: starting rate 5.500 percent, margin 2.500 points, first-change cap 2.00 points, later-change cap 1.50 points, lifetime cap 4.00 points. None of these is a published program term.

| Adjustment | Index published 45 days earlier | Index increased by margin | Rounded to nearest 0.125 | Allowed range | New note rate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| First | 4.912 | 7.412 | 7.375 | 3.500 to 7.500 (prior 5.500, cap 2.00) | 7.375 |
| Second | 3.200 | 5.700 | 5.750 | 5.875 to 8.875 (prior 7.375, cap 1.50) | 5.875 |

In both rows the lifetime ceiling of 9.500 (5.500 increased by 4.00) and the floor of 2.500 (the margin) are respected. In the second row the rounded value falls below what the later-change cap allows, so the rate settles at the lowest permitted level, 5.875.

## Points of judgement

**Rounding in the first row.** 7.412 lies 0.037 above 7.375 and 0.088 below 7.500; the nearest multiple of 0.125 is therefore 7.375.

**Can the rate ever go below the margin?** No, even when the index is very low.
